note.question: Which economically and computationally complex features of the FCC spectrum incentive auction materially improved procurement cost and allocative efficiency?
note.overview: The paper evaluates a complex reverse-auction mechanism. Truthful myopic bidding is obviously dominant in the UHF-only special case; when VHF options are present, no full equilibrium bidding strategy is known, so the quantitative evaluation explicitly assumes truthful myopic behavior rather than claiming an equilibrium of the complete FCC game.

models.method: Recognizing that stations’ incentives are unaffected by the order in which their feasibility checks are performed, we propose an alternate bid processing algorithm (dubbed “first to finish”) that aims to order feasibility checks in ascending order of their runtimes, ensuring that a round never terminates early unless all feasibility problems have been solved.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Within a reverse-auction stage, the clock descends and each active station chooses among remaining broadcasting options or exits; the feasibility checker freezes stations that cannot be repacked with prior exits. If forward revenue covers reverse costs the process stops; otherwise a new reverse stage begins at a lower clearing target. Station exit and freezing decisions interact through geographic interference constraints. VHF options expand feasible trades but add a strategic choice absent from the simple clock.
